what: An example wing made for the demo: a tapered, swept half wing that ends in a blended winglet, two skins over two spar webs and eleven ribs

wing.sweep_measures: how far aft of the root's leading edge the tip's leading edge lies, along x

measures.cant: degrees the fin leans up from the wing's plane, turned about the chord (x); 90 would stand upright
measures.radius: mm, the arc the chord line turns through in the bend, seen along x
measures.fin: mm, the fin's length along its own span line, from the end of the bend to its tip
measures.sweep: mm, how far aft of the wing tip's leading edge the fin tip's leading edge lies, along x
measures.tip_chord: mm, the chord at the fin's tip
measures.rise: mm, how far the fin tip's chord line stands above the wing's (z = 0)
measures.reach: mm, how far outboard of the tip rib the fin tip's chord line lies, along y
measures.ribs: mm out along the span line from the tip rib: the rib where the bend ends and the rib that closes the fin's tip
measures.stations: one row a station outboard of the tip rib: mm out along the span line from the tip rib; the leading edge's x, y and z; the chord, which runs along x; the degrees the section is turned up about x

load.how: Pushed up at the 16 points where the 2 spars meet the upper skin at the wing's 8 ribs outboard of the root, the tip rib the last of them, in equal shares; none on the winglet; the root is held.
